video_title: Richard Wolff, Cornel West, & Norman Finkelstein: America Is in DENIAL | On Mamdani, Tucker, & Trump
gist: Wolff, West and Finkelstein discuss who rules America, arguing for a hollowed-out labor base, an unaccountable Mamdani administration, a fracturing Trump coalition, and structural economic decline, with Wolff on German energy costs and China's hybrid model. The conversation is political and ideological, with limited hard data.

insights.claim: The US no longer has a working class in the classical sense: only about 8% of workers are unionized, likely falling to 6%, workers are atomized into gigs, and they no longer sit at the core of the economy.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Weak labor power means little organized pressure on wages or policy, which supports capital-favoring outcomes.
insights.quote: 8% of American workers are currently unionized and probably next year will be down to 6%

insights.claim: Even a mass strike at Amazon would not bring the system down because retail competitors would absorb the slack, so workers no longer hold structural leverage.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Platform concentration does not translate into labor bargaining power; strike risk to large retailers is low.

insights.claim: Wolff argues the left could organize gig workers into unions, noting capitalism turned salaried union workers into individual gig sellers and the next step could reverse that, as the CIO did relative to the AFL in the 1930s.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: A gig-worker organizing wave would be a labor-cost risk for platform companies.

insights.claim: Finkelstein rejects gig organizing as unrealistic, arguing solidarity formed through decades in huge factories like Ford, GM and the mines cannot be recreated among gig workers.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Skeptic view implies platform labor costs stay structurally low.
insights.quote: None of that is coming back.

insights.claim: Without membership institutions such as unions, elected officials face no accountability; Finkelstein cites Mamdani's undefended decisions as the result.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Political outcomes track organized pressure, not election results alone.

themes.theme: Mamdani and the limits of electoral socialism

insights.claim: Finkelstein criticizes NYC mayor Mamdani for retaining police commissioner Jessica Tisch, backing Hakeem Jeffries, and skipping the demonstration when Netanyahu visited the UN, without explaining the reversals to the 90,000 door-knockers.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Signals Mamdani is governing as an institutional Democrat, lowering odds of radical NYC fiscal or real-estate policy.

insights.claim: Finkelstein says the 90,000 door-knockers wanted a public works jobs program and a doubled minimum wage, not free buses, so Mamdani's platform of rent stabilization, free buses, and city grocery stores was less radical than expected.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Gap between voter expectations and the platform raises disillusionment risk and pressure for larger labor-market intervention.

insights.claim: West predicts Mamdani, being a bona fide Democratic Party member allied with the governor and Jeffries, could become a Muslim version of Obama, and says left populism will be weak if he does not confront police and gentrification issues.
insights.speaker: Cornel West
insights.so_what: Expect Mamdani to stay within the Democratic establishment, limiting disruption to NYC real estate and business interests.

insights.claim: West says DSA's base has shifted from industrial workers and UAW ties in the early days to educated gentrifiers focused on affordability, which black New Yorkers perceive as the people pushing them out.
insights.speaker: Cornel West
insights.so_what: Affordability politics are driven by a professional-class base, shaping which housing and cost-of-living policies advance.

insights.claim: Wolff says DSA mastered trial and error and campaigning and beat an old hack, but its challenge is the day after election: no institutions exist to hold elected members accountable.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Left electoral wins may not translate into policy delivery.

insights.claim: Wolff argues the US inherited the other powers' colonial networks after WWII because it was never bombed and lost no colonies, producing an unprecedented concentration of wealth, and that the world is now in an anticolonial era increasingly aimed at the US as the last big colonial power.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Frames a multi-decade erosion of US economic dominance, not a cyclical dip.

insights.claim: Wolff says Europe is becoming the junior partner and a tourist attraction, and its leaders (Macron, Merz, and Burnham who replaced Starmer) are as unpopular as Trump.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: European political fragility raises policy and euro-area risk.

insights.claim: Wolff says WWII deaths of 27 million Russians versus 400,000 Americans show the US escaped the carnage that destroyed other imperial powers.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Context for US postwar dominance.

insights.claim: Wolff argues the old postwar bargain has inverted: the system worked for roughly 80% in the 1960s, whereas now it works for about 20% and fails 80%, which drives support for rightist parties.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Broad economic precarity is the structural driver of populist political risk.

insights.claim: West says America is the only one of roughly 70 empires in history that denies it is an empire, and cites about 800 military bases and special operations units in 101 countries as evidence.
insights.speaker: Cornel West
insights.so_what: Persistent imperial overextension is a long-term fiscal and geopolitical burden.

themes.theme: Trump, MAGA, and a right in fracture

insights.claim: Wolff predicts the working class will move left, as it did in the 1930s, once the right fails to deliver jobs and income and Social Security comes under strain.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: If voters drift left on economic grievances, expect policy risk around taxes, labor and entitlements.

insights.claim: Wolff says Trump promised to bring back manufacturing and has not delivered it, and that even right-wing colleagues agree.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Reshoring promises have not produced results, per this speaker.

insights.claim: West says Trump is running out of gas, evidenced by Tucker Carlson and Marjorie Taylor Greene leaving the ship, with Carlson calling for Trump's removal under the 25th Amendment.
insights.speaker: Cornel West
insights.so_what: Fracture within MAGA could reshape Republican coalition and 2028 positioning.

insights.claim: Finkelstein predicts 25,000 potential Trumps waiting in the wings, naming Tucker Carlson as a possible next one, and notes Carlson's turn on Gaza and religion.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: A populist successor could continue the same policy regime post-Trump.

insights.claim: West says Trump's appeal to MAGA is that he is despised by liberal elites and behaves unlike the Bush or Clinton families, so billionaire status did not matter.
insights.speaker: Cornel West
insights.so_what: Anti-elite identification, not policy, anchors his base.

insights.claim: Wolff says a government job guarantee would pay for itself because hired workers produce more value than they are paid, and the obstacle is political rather than economic.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: A heterodox claim; policy feasibility rests on political will, not the budget.
insights.quote: this is not an economic problem.

insights.claim: Wolff says immigrants are saving American capitalism because the US does not reproduce its population and immigrant workers produce surplus that funds the system.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Immigration restriction implies labor-supply and growth headwinds.
insights.quote: We do not reproduce our population in this country.

insights.claim: Finkelstein calls mass deportation a form of state terrorism and refuses to work with Tucker Carlson while he advocates it, though he would let Carlson march on Gaza.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Left-right alliances on Gaza are limited by immigration.

insights.claim: Wolff says German postwar prosperity (the Wirtschaftswunder) rested on cheap Soviet and Russian oil and gas; cutting it off means paying three to four times more to buy US energy, making Germany high-cost against Chinese manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: Explains German industrial decline and rise of AfD-type politics; energy cost is the key variable for European industry.

insights.claim: Wolff predicts Germany's AfD, which proposes ending Ukraine support and resetting relations with Russia, would put Germans back to work through a Russia deal, making Russians heroes and changing European and US politics.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: A German policy pivot toward Russian energy would reshape European energy markets and sanctions.

insights.claim: Wolff describes China's economy as a hybrid of about half private capital (Chinese and foreign) and half state-owned, and says it made one of the poorest countries a colossus without Marshall Plan money.
insights.speaker: Richard Wolff
insights.so_what: China's mixed model has outperformed, shaping competitive dynamics against Western manufacturers.

insights.claim: Finkelstein says reversing to the old made-in-USA prosperity is not realistic, and Wolff agrees you cannot go back but can move to new directions.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Manufacturing reshoring faces structural limits.

insights.claim: Finkelstein says elite institutions such as universities and hospitals respond to wrongdoing by protecting reputation, with reports dissolving in the ether of denial.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Institutions optimize for image over accountability.
insights.quote: dissolved in the ether of denial

insights.claim: Finkelstein says US media frames the US and Israel attacks on Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine as unprovoked aggression while ignoring 20 years of NATO eastward expansion.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Mainstream narratives may understate Russian security grievances.

insights.claim: Finkelstein says he was not surprised universities capitulated in spring 2024 to the Gaza encampments and funding threats, and compares it to law firms like Paul Weiss capitulating to the Trump administration.
insights.speaker: Norman Finkelstein
insights.so_what: Institutions with federal funding exposure capitulate quickly under pressure.

insights.claim: West says Larry Summers shut out African-American studies and that black Harvard intellectuals became brands and celebrities rather than freedom fighters.
insights.speaker: Cornel West
insights.so_what: Context on commodification of dissent.
